collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager's pebble piles for fishing and farming come out exactly even: count again, or kick the piles over.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is trying to decide whether to switch from fishing to farming. (subject.He/she) has made two piles of pebbles: one pebble for each good reason for fishing, and one for each good reason for farming. (friend) wanders by and looks at the piles. They are exactly the same size.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) counts again, carefully. Still the same. (subject.He/she) adds one pebble to fishing \("I like the boats"\). Then one to farming \("No sharks"\). Then one to fishing \("I'm good at it"\). (friend) watches this for a while. "Do you want me to go and get more pebbles?" (friend.he/she) asks. "Yes," says (subject), seriously. (subject.He/she) still hasn't decided by nightfall. (subject.He/she) has a lot of pebbles, though.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) looks at the two equal piles, then kicks them both over. "Fishing," (subject.he/she) says. "I just want to keep fishing." (friend) raises an eyebrow. "So what were the pebbles for?" "To find out that I didn't want to stop," says (subject), and goes back to (subject.his/her) nets.
